claims.text: A heat pump moves heat rather than making it, so it delivers more heat energy than the electricity it uses
claims.note: UK quasi-experiment on 1,321 Octopus Energy heat pump adopters: gas use fell 9,351 kWh/yr while electricity rose 3,080 kWh/yr, so the heat pump replaced gas using only about 30% of the energy, in line with roughly 300% efficiency.

claims.text: Air sealing and insulation should come before or alongside a heat pump
claims.note: ResStock modelling: envelope upgrades cut bill-increase cases (39% to 19% with minimum-efficiency units) and shrink heat pump capacity, but add about $9,000 so the net upfront cost rises, raising positive-NPV share slightly in cold climates and lowering it in warmer ones.

claims.text: Whether a heat pump is cheaper to run than gas depends mainly on local electricity and gas prices
claims.note: LBNL retrofit database (1,739 projects): about 70 electrification projects in states with high electricity costs raised household energy costs, and the authors conclude savings must be judged state by state given the variation in gas and electricity prices.

claims.text: Many installers charge heat pump prices far above the equipment and labor cost
claims.note: Installed heat pump prices are high and opaque relative to equipment cost, but evidence on systematic markups beyond labor, permits and overhead is mostly anecdotal.

claims.text: Ducted heat pumps can often use a home's existing ductwork
claims.note: Ducted heat pumps commonly replace a central AC condenser and coil on existing ducts, though some duct systems need changes.

claims.text: An air conditioner is a heat pump that only runs in one direction
claims.note: RMI describes heat pumps as working like air conditioners in summer and running in reverse in winter, so an air conditioner is the one-direction case.

claims.text: Existing ductwork can be too small for the airflow a heat pump needs
claims.note: Heat pumps need about 400 cfm/ton versus about 156 for non-condensing furnaces because of cooler supply air, and one expert estimates most duct systems handle only 2-3 tons of airflow.

claims.text: Contractors routinely oversize heating and cooling equipment
claims.note: Field studies of US residential HVAC commonly find furnaces and ACs sized well above calculated design loads.

claims.text: Heat pump efficiency and capacity fall as the outdoor temperature drops
claims.note: Measured heat-pump-only cycles averaged COP about 1.3 at the 10F change point rising to 3.0-4.5 at 50-60F; outdoor temperature had the largest effect on COP across six Minnesota sites.

claims.text: Installers can absorb heat pump rebates by raising their quotes
claims.note: Studies of energy-efficiency subsidies find some pass-through to sellers, but most rebate value usually reaches buyers.

claims.text: Electric resistance heat costs far more to run than a heat pump
claims.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see positive bill savings in 95-100% of cases with median savings of $300-$650 a year at any efficiency level.

claims.text: Defrost cycles reduce a heat pump's output and efficiency in cold, humid weather
claims.note: Defrost cut ccASHP COP at site 2 (e.g. 1.86 to 1.65 at 10-20F), drove backup energy use between the 10F changeover and 40F, and eliminating it would have raised annual energy savings by 8.3%.

claims.text: Cold-climate heat pumps often rely on backup resistance heat in the coldest weather, which raises bills
claims.note: Auxiliary heat runtime generally rose in colder bins and heavy use cut system COP over 30% at two sites, but the heavy users were undersized or faulty while six sites used little auxiliary heat.

claims.text: Heat pumps cut a home's carbon emissions compared with gas heating, even on today's grid
claims.note: On the 2024 UK grid, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump cut household energy CO2eq by about 1.16 t/yr, 36% of the pre-adoption footprint, from measured consumption changes and government emission factors.

claims.text: Choosing a heat pump instead of a new central air conditioner adds efficient heating for little extra cost
claims.note: Wholesale heat pumps cost only $200-$500 more than equivalent ACs, but heat pumps sized to fully electrify heating often cost more to install than AC plus furnace because of larger capacity, wiring and panel upgrades.

claims.text: Modern cold-climate heat pumps keep heating well below 0°F
claims.note: A ductless cold-climate unit delivered a consistent median capacity from 10F to -15F and kept operating to -25F at reduced capacity, though the authors say it needs backup below -15F; one monitored unit.

claims.text: Widespread backup resistance heat in extreme cold strains the electric grid
claims.note: At 100% adoption, with supplemental heat modelled as resistance, cities covering 44% of the housing stock (mostly cold climates) see peak residential demand more than double.

claims.text: Heat pumps deliver cooler supply air than a gas furnace, which some people find less comfortable
claims.note: Heat pump supply air rarely exceeded 100F (often around 80F) versus about 120F for fossil furnaces; occupant comfort was not measured.

claims.text: A dual-fuel system (heat pump with a gas furnace backup) is cheaper to run than either alone in cold climates
claims.note: With a well-set changeover temperature dual fuel can beat either fuel alone, but the saving over gas alone is small where gas is cheap and it needs two systems.

claims.text: From 2023 through 2025 a federal tax credit covered 30% of a qualifying heat pump, up to $2,000
claims.note: IRS 25C page: from 2023 the credit equals 30% of qualified expenses, with a $2,000-per-year cap for qualified heat pumps (installation labor included).

claims.text: Ground-source (geothermal) heat pumps run cheaper but cost much more to install than air-source
claims.note: RMI notes that ground-source heat pumps use less energy on the coldest days because ground temperature stays moderate, but have historically cost significantly more than air-source because of drilling.

claims.text: Replacing a working gas furnace with a heat pump rarely pays back on energy savings alone
claims.note: In RMI's four-city model at 2018 prices, homes with gas heat that only need a new furnace usually pay more over 15 years to electrify than to stay on gas, even when the furnace is being replaced anyway (an advocacy model of a few cities).

claims.text: Pairing a heat pump with rooftop solar makes it much cheaper to run
claims.note: Solar lowers the effective electricity price, but winter heating demand peaks when solar output is lowest, so the gain depends on net metering terms.

claims.text: A federal tax credit for heat pumps is available for installations in 2026
claims.note: IRS fact sheet on the 2025 budget law (OBBB): the 25C home improvement credit is not allowed for property placed in service after December 31, 2025, and the 25D clean energy credit for expenditures after that date, so no federal heat pump credit applies to 2026 installs.

claims.text: Federal Inflation Reduction Act rebates for heat pumps are available to most homeowners
claims.note: DOE Program Notice 26-2: the federal electrification rebate no longer funds replacing non-electric (gas, oil, propane) heating, which rules out most homes that would switch to a heat pump; it is also an income-limited program run by the states.

claims.text: Federal heat pump rebates for low- and moderate-income households depend on slow state-by-state rollout
claims.note: As of Feb 2026, the National Housing Trust tracker shows most states' HEAR and HER programs only conditionally approved with no expected launch date (e.g. Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas), and others partly launched or in pilots, three-plus years after the 2022 law.

claims.text: State and utility heat pump rebates were not affected by the 2025 federal budget law
claims.note: State and utility programs are funded separately (ratepayers, state budgets) and the budget law did not repeal them.

claims.text: Heat pumps installed in 2025 can still get the federal credit on the 2025 tax return
claims.note: IRS 25C page: the credit can be claimed for improvements made through December 31, 2025, and is claimed for the tax year the property is installed.

claims.text: The federal 30% credit for geothermal heat pumps ended after 2025
claims.note: IRS: the 25D residential clean energy credit is not allowed for expenditures after December 31, 2025, and an expenditure counts only when installation is completed; geothermal heat pumps fall under 25D, though this fact sheet does not name them or the 30% rate.

claims.text: High electricity prices relative to gas make heat pumps more expensive to run than gas boilers or furnaces
claims.note: UK heat pump households (measured consumption times retail prices) pay about £190/yr more to run a heat pump than a gas boiler at Octopus standard rates (£323 at government 2024 prices), with electricity about 4x the price of gas per kWh; disconnecting from gas trims about £100/yr off the gap.

claims.text: Time-of-use or heat-pump electricity tariffs make heat pumps cheaper to run
claims.note: Staggered-adoption study of 6,631 UK households: switching to Octopus's Cosy heat pump time-of-use tariff saved about £318/yr (about 18% of the electricity bill), £78 from the tariff structure alone and £240 from shifting load; savings are vs the same supplier's flat tariff, and the authors are linked to Octopus.

claims.text: Home batteries charged off-peak pay back within a few years by cutting heat pump running costs
claims.note: Independent estimates of home battery payback from tariff arbitrage are typically closer to a decade, not a few years.

claims.text: Smart control apps that run a heat pump in cheap tariff hours cut its running costs substantially
claims.note: RMI finds that shifting load into cheap hours saves a lot for water heating ($154 to $48 a year in Houston) but only a few dollars a year for space heating, because a house cannot be overheated or hold heat like a tank.

claims.text: Heating with a heat pump costs less than heating with a natural gas furnace
claims.note: In the UK at 2024 prices on a standard flat tariff, heat pumps cost about £190 more per year to run than the gas boilers they replaced (boilers, not furnaces); only a heat pump time-of-use tariff reverses this.

claims.text: Switching to a heat pump cuts heating bills by half or more
claims.note: In the UK, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump raised measured running costs by about £190/yr on a standard tariff, far from halving bills, even though energy use fell 40%.

claims.text: Oversized or poorly installed heat pumps cost more to run and deliver less comfort
claims.note: Field studies link poor sizing, charge, airflow and commissioning to substantially lower measured efficiency.

claims.text: In cold climates a heat pump sized for the cooling load cannot carry the full heating load
claims.note: Sizing for heating added about one ton over cooling sizing; for an example home a 2-ton (cooling-sized) unit would hand off to the furnace at 27F versus 14F for 3-ton and 5F for 4-ton.

claims.text: A dual-fuel system lets a smaller heat pump handle most heating while a furnace covers the coldest days
claims.note: Most heating hours occur at mild temperatures, so a heat pump sized below the design load still covers most of the season's heat.

claims.text: Heat pump installation quotes vary widely between contractors for similar equipment
claims.note: Quote comparisons and program data show installed heat pump prices for similar homes varying by multiples between contractors.

claims.text: Switching from gas to a heat pump raises the household's energy bills
claims.note: UK households switching from gas boilers see running costs about £190/yr higher on a standard tariff (about £83 after dropping the gas standing charge), so bills do rise modestly; but the same paper finds a heat pump time-of-use tariff saves about £318/yr, enough to reverse the rise.

claims.text: Heat pumps need a home to be well insulated to work economically
claims.note: The UK Electrification of Heat trial installed heat pumps in every housing type, including old, poorly insulated homes, with similar efficiency; insulation lowers cost but is not a prerequisite.

claims.text: Heat pumps on radiator systems often need larger radiators to run efficiently
claims.note: Heat pumps are efficient at low flow temperatures, so radiators sized for hot boiler water often need enlarging.

claims.text: A heat pump costs more to buy and install than a gas furnace
claims.note: LBNL: among 2,298 HVAC measures, fuel-fired heating systems averaged $3,000 less than heat pump installations (heat pump median $8,027 vs furnace median $5,025 in 2019 dollars), though heat pumps also provide cooling.

claims.text: Many heat pump owners end up with high bills and a colder house
claims.note: Surveys of UK and US heat pump owners find satisfaction similar to or higher than gas boiler owners.

claims.text: The UK Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant requires removing the existing gas boiler
claims.note: BUS rules require the heat pump to replace the fossil fuel system fully; hybrid systems are not eligible.

claims.text: Heat pump outdoor units are noisy enough to cause neighbour complaints
claims.note: Modern units are typically around 40-60 dB at a few metres and complaints are uncommon, though poorly placed units can bother neighbours.

claims.text: Natural gas costs much less than electricity per unit of energy delivered to the home
claims.note: At 2024 US average residential prices electricity costs $48.30/MMBtu versus $14.00 for gas, a ratio of 3.45 (state range 1.69 Florida to 6.42 Alaska).

claims.text: Heat pumps do not work in very cold climates
claims.note: In monitored Minnesota homes cold-climate ASHPs cut heating costs 30-56%; cold weather raised backup and defrost use and lowered heat pump performance but overall system efficiencies remained high.

claims.text: Heat pumps are being used successfully in cold countries like Norway and Canada
claims.note: Heat pumps heat a large share of homes in Norway, Sweden and Finland and are spreading in Canada and Maine.

claims.text: A heat pump cools as efficiently as a comparable central air conditioner
claims.note: A heat pump is the same refrigeration machine as an AC, and inverter models often have higher SEER2 ratings than typical installed ACs.

claims.text: The UK Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant covers most of a typical air-source heat pump installation
claims.note: MCS data put the average UK air-source installation at £12,713 after the grant rose to £7,500, so the grant covered about 59% and left about £5,213 to the household.

claims.text: A heat pump costs less to run than heating with oil, propane or electric resistance
claims.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see lower bills in 95-100% of cases (median $300-$650/yr); 73-86% without AC; still 87-99% (propane) and 66-100% (oil) at 2019 prices.

claims.text: Heat pumps save the most money in homes now heated with oil, propane or electric resistance
claims.note: Median bill savings of $300-$650/yr for electric, oil and propane homes with AC compare with -$70 to $380/yr for gas homes with AC.

claims.text: Replacing an oil furnace with a heat pump pays back within a few years
claims.note: When an oil furnace needs replacing anyway, the incremental cost often pays back in about five to ten years, depending on oil prices and climate.

claims.text: A heat pump replaces both the furnace and the air conditioner with one system
claims.note: Edwards explains that heat pumps heat and, by reversing the refrigerant, cool, replacing the separate furnace and air conditioner of a conventional system.

claims.text: Payback for a heat pump varies widely with climate, fuel prices and the equipment it replaces
claims.note: Bill savings vary by climate, prices and housing stock across locations, and vary even more between the 5th and 95th percentiles within one location.

claims.text: Heat pumps need more maintenance or repairs than gas furnaces
claims.note: Seven homeowners needed contractor visits, mostly minor control, sensor or condensate issues fixed in one visit, and the team judged this not atypical compared with their previous systems; the units were prototypes and the sample was small.

claims.text: Heat pumps are a better fit than gas furnaces in mild climates
claims.note: Mild (mixed and coastal) climates have the greatest heat pump potential, and any beneficial gas replacement is in hot or mild climates; cold climates see the smallest benefit.

claims.text: Heat pump defrost cycles release meltwater that can ice driveways and walkways
claims.note: Defrost meltwater drains from the outdoor unit and can refreeze on paved surfaces in sub-freezing weather.

claims.text: A heat pump costs about the same as a central air conditioner of the same capacity
claims.note: Standard heat pumps usually cost modestly more than a same-size AC, while cold-climate variable-speed models cost several thousand more.

claims.text: Switching to a heat pump substantially lowers monthly energy bills
claims.note: Edwards finds 19% of households would pay more and 28% show no clear change with a heat pump, so substantial bill cuts are not general.

claims.text: HVAC equipment prices keep rising, so waiting to buy a heat pump costs more
claims.note: HVAC equipment prices rose sharply in 2021-2025 with inflation and the refrigerant transition, but future prices and incentives are uncertain.

claims.text: Claiming a heat pump incentive requires proof that the installed equipment pairing meets the efficiency standard
claims.note: Federal and most utility incentives require the matched indoor and outdoor units to meet efficiency tiers, usually shown by an AHRI certificate.

claims.text: From 2023 through 2025 a federal tax credit covered part of the cost of a home energy audit
claims.note: IRS 25C page: a home energy audit of the main home may qualify for a credit of up to $150 if it meets the written-report and qualified-auditor requirements.

claims.text: Well-installed air-source heat pumps reach seasonal efficiencies around four in real homes
claims.note: Across 166 metered indoor units of whole-home systems in Maine, the combined field-metered heating COP over the season was 3.15 including defrost, about 2 at -10F, not around four (a cold climate; milder climates would score higher).

claims.text: With electric backup, the heat pump keeps running alongside the heat strips to cut backup use
claims.note: Below the switchover temperature the cold-climate units mostly ran heat pump plus staged auxiliary heat (supplemental mode), with auxiliary-only operation minimal above 0 F, and staging used the smallest element needed.

claims.text: Setting an auxiliary heat lockout temperature keeps backup strip heat from running in mild weather
claims.note: Lockout controls prevent strip heat above a set outdoor temperature, a requirement in the IECC.

claims.text: A faulty heat pump can run unnoticed on backup resistance heat and send bills soaring
claims.note: At Site 2 a control or sensor fault left the compressor idle from February 16 to April 11 while resistance heat carried the home, and the homeowner did not notice; auxiliary energy exceeded compressor energy.

claims.text: Running a heat pump steadily at low flow temperature costs less than heating in short bursts
claims.note: Monitored UK heat pumps reach higher COPs with weather compensation and continuous low-temperature running, though setbacks can still save in leaky homes.

claims.text: A vetted-contractor program with negotiated pricing lowers heat pump installation costs
claims.note: LBNL: the CEE program's fixed contractor network working at pre-agreed costs 'reduces measure costs' and keeps comprehensive projects low-cost, and the PAYS program with fixed contractor networks and streamlined scopes also lowered costs (observational program comparison).

claims.text: A properly sized inverter heat pump can heat a home at its design temperature without backup resistance heat
claims.note: Field reports show variable-speed units covering full load at moderate design temperatures, but not in very cold climates or leaky homes.

claims.text: Inverter heat pumps defrost faster than single-stage heat pumps
claims.note: Defrost behaviour varies by control strategy; no independent comparison is widely available.

claims.text: Through 2025 a federal tax credit covered 30% of a geothermal heat pump's installed cost with no cap
claims.note: The 25D residential clean energy credit covered 30% of ground-source heat pump costs without a dollar cap until it ended after 2025.

claims.text: State and utility rebates can cover a large share of a heat pump's cost
claims.note: Some states and utilities pay thousands of dollars, but programs vary widely and many areas offer little.

claims.text: Proper sizing from a load calculation matters more than brand
claims.note: Installation and sizing faults affect performance more than brand differences among major manufacturers, but evidence is mostly practitioner consensus.

claims.text: Inverter-driven heat pumps run more efficiently and quietly than single-stage units
claims.note: Variable-speed compressors have higher SEER2/HSPF2 ratings and lower sound levels at part load.

claims.text: The R-410A refrigerant phase-down does not require replacing a working system
claims.note: The AIM Act phase-down limits new equipment production; existing systems can still be serviced with R-410A.

claims.text: A heat pump with an electric air handler costs less to install than a dual-fuel system with a furnace
claims.note: An air handler is usually cheaper than a furnace plus coil, but a dual-fuel retrofit that keeps a working furnace can cost less.

claims.text: Burning gas in a power plant to run a heat pump delivers more heat than burning it in a home furnace
claims.note: RMI's water-heating example finds a heat pump water heater powered by a combined-cycle gas plant burns less gas and emits less than a gas-fired water heater, so burning gas at the plant is more efficient than burning it at home.

claims.text: A heat pump still uses less energy than resistance heat even in very cold weather
claims.note: Metered COP averaged 2 at -10F across 166 units in Maine homes, so even in very cold weather the heat pumps used about half the electricity resistance heat would.

claims.text: A cold-climate heat pump needs backup heat only on a few of the coldest days of the year
claims.note: Field studies in cold climates show backup covering a small share of heat, but more in very cold places or with poor controls.

claims.text: Air-to-air heat pumps cost far less to install than air-to-water systems
claims.note: In the UK, ductless air-to-air installs typically cost a fraction of air-to-water systems with cylinders and radiator upgrades.

claims.text: A heat pump pays for itself through lower energy bills within a few years
claims.note: Even over 16 years, unsubsidized NPV is positive for only 55% (minimum), 41% (medium) and 21% (high-efficiency) of homes, far from a few-year payback for all.

claims.text: A heat pump can be added alongside an existing furnace to cut fuel use
claims.note: Mini-splits added alongside existing heating cut the baseline fuel by about 3.8-4.7 MMBtu per unit in winter 2016 on average, at a cost of about 763 kWh of electricity.

claims.text: Geothermal heat pumps run best with little or no thermostat setback
claims.note: Manufacturers recommend minimal setback because recovery from deep setbacks can trigger backup heat and offsets savings.

claims.text: A geothermal desuperheater preheats domestic hot water using waste heat
claims.note: Desuperheaters recover compressor heat to preheat water, mainly during cooling season.

claims.text: Running a heat pump on emergency heat instead of the heat pump sharply raises electric bills
claims.note: Emergency mode runs only resistance heat at COP 1, roughly two to three times the cost of heat pump operation.

claims.text: Backup heat should be sized to cover the gap at design temperature, not the full heating load
claims.note: ACCA guidance sizes supplemental heat to the shortfall, though some codes or owners want full emergency backup.

claims.text: Geothermal heat pumps rarely pay back their extra cost over an efficient air-source heat pump
claims.note: With modern cold-climate air-source units, the running-cost gap is small relative to the installation premium unless incentives are large.

claims.text: In off-grid homes a geothermal heat pump can cost less overall by shrinking the solar and battery system needed
claims.note: Based on one builder's modelled costs, not independently measured.

claims.text: Inverter heat pumps keep far more of their heating capacity in cold weather than single-stage units
claims.note: AHRI performance data show variable-speed cold-climate units retaining 70-100% capacity at 5°F versus about half for basic single-stage units.

claims.text: A premium inverter heat pump's energy savings repay its higher price over a basic single-stage system
claims.note: Medium and high-efficiency variable-speed units save more on bills, but their higher upfront costs cut positive unsubsidized NPV from 55% (minimum single-speed) to 41% and 21% (38% if high-efficiency costs are overestimated).

claims.text: Variable-speed heat pumps dehumidify better than single-stage systems
claims.note: Longer low-speed run times can remove more moisture, but it depends on airflow settings and controls.

claims.text: HVAC replacement prices rose sharply in recent years
claims.note: Producer price indexes and refrigerant transitions drove double-digit HVAC equipment and install price increases since 2020.

claims.text: Replacing HVAC equipment before it fails, in the off season, gets a lower price
claims.note: Planned replacement allows comparing bids and seasonal promotions, but discounts are anecdotal and vary.

claims.text: Contractors discount replacing the furnace and air conditioner together
claims.note: Bundle pricing is a contractor practice with no independent data on its size.

claims.text: From 2023 through 2025 a federal tax credit covered up to $600 of a high-efficiency central air conditioner
claims.note: IRS 25C page: central air conditioners meeting the CEE highest non-advanced tier qualify as residential energy property for a credit of up to $600 per item.

claims.text: A low-cost ductless mini-split can heat a space in single-digit outdoor temperatures
claims.note: Many inexpensive inverter mini-splits are rated to operate below 5°F, though at reduced capacity.

claims.text: Snow and ice buildup on the outdoor unit can stop a heat pump from heating
claims.note: In the snowy 2015 winter several outdoor units were encased in snow or ice and, without clearance, 'could not provide heating'; buried units for up to a month also visibly lowered that winter's measured efficiencies.

claims.text: A home's true heating load can be estimated from smart thermostat runtime on a cold day
claims.note: Runtime-based load estimation is an established method for single-stage equipment, though less accurate for multistage or zoned systems.

claims.text: Installing a heat pump can require costly electrical panel or service upgrades
claims.note: Across 21 installs, 38% needed a new panel, 24% a service line upgrade and 90% new breakers for auxiliary heat; electrical upgrades alone cost $3,750-$8,970 in labour and materials.

claims.text: Radiator size and flow temperature decide whether a heat pump costs less to run than a gas boiler
claims.note: Larger emitters allow lower flow temperatures and higher COP, but the electricity-to-gas price ratio is just as decisive.

claims.text: The UK Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant pays £7,500 toward a heat pump installation
claims.note: The UK Boiler Upgrade Scheme started in May 2022 at £5,000 per air-source heat pump and rose to £7,500 from 23 October 2023.

claims.text: Heat pump installation prices will fall to match gas boilers as sales scale up
claims.note: The authors say heat pump learning rates are not established and UK evidence shows very small or zero price declines so far, possibly masked by inflation, constrained supply or harder homes, so whether prices will fall is open.

claims.text: Removing the gas connection saves its fixed monthly charge
claims.note: Homes that convert all gas end uses and shut off service no longer pay the fixed charge (median $11.25/month in 2015, up to $34-$65 in Chicago and NYC); dropping it raises gas homes with positive savings from 32-92% to 49-97%.

claims.text: Heat pumps last about as long as furnaces and air conditioners
claims.note: Heat pumps typically last 12-15 years, similar to central ACs but shorter than many gas furnaces.

claims.text: A gas furnace can run on a small generator during a power outage while a heat pump cannot
claims.note: A gas furnace's blower draws a few hundred watts, while a heat pump with strip heat needs several kilowatts at 240V.

claims.text: The federal heat pump tax credit was nonrefundable, so it gave nothing to households without tax liability
claims.note: IRS 25C page: the credit is nonrefundable, so you cannot get back more than you owe in taxes and cannot carry excess forward.

claims.text: Replacing an old single-stage air conditioner with an inverter heat pump cuts cooling costs substantially
claims.note: Moving from SEER 13 to a high-SEER inverter unit can cut cooling energy roughly 25-40% on paper, but measured savings are often smaller.

claims.text: Heat pumps heat radiators to lower temperatures than gas or oil boilers
claims.note: Standard air-to-water heat pumps run most efficiently at 35-55°C flow versus 60-80°C for typical boilers, though high-temperature models exist.

claims.text: Surveys showing heat pump owners are as satisfied as gas boiler owners rely on unrepresentative samples
claims.note: The Nesta survey groups differed in property type and were self-selected, though monitored trials also report high satisfaction.

claims.text: Since mid-2026 the federal electric appliance rebate no longer pays to replace gas or oil heating with a heat pump
claims.note: DOE Program Notice 26-2 (effective May 29, 2026) removes fuel-switching from the HEEHR (formerly HEAR) rebate, allowing HVAC rebates only for replacing existing electric equipment; launched programs must comply within three months, though existing reservations can still be honored.

claims.text: The federal whole-home efficiency rebate still pays toward a heat pump that replaces gas heating
claims.note: HOMES is fuel-neutral and performance-based by design, but state availability and any 2026 changes are unverified.

claims.text: Most federal home energy tax credit claims went to higher-income households
claims.note: CRS and Treasury data show residential energy credits were disproportionately claimed by households with incomes above $100,000.

claims.text: Heat pumps outsell gas furnaces in the US
claims.note: AHRI shipment data show air-source heat pump shipments exceeding gas furnace shipments each year since 2022.

claims.text: Inverter heat pumps run quieter than furnaces and older air conditioners
claims.note: Inverter outdoor units are quiet at low speed, but comparing them with mostly indoor furnaces is not like-for-like.

claims.text: Backup resistance heat strips use less electricity than letting the heat pump run longer to catch up
claims.note: The report says excessive auxiliary resistance runtime is costly and significant energy waste, to be minimized by proper heat pump sizing and controls (elsewhere it notes the auxiliary heater runs at COP 1).

claims.text: Canada's federal program pays up to $10,000 to switch oil-heated homes to a heat pump
claims.note: The federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program pays up to $10,000 upfront for cold-climate air-source heat pumps (as of 2023; landlords and renters ineligible).

claims.text: A heat pump removes the carbon monoxide risk of combustion heating
claims.note: An electric heat pump has no combustion, so it removes that carbon monoxide source, though other gas appliances may remain.

claims.text: Ductless heat pumps allow room-by-room temperature control
claims.note: Each ductless indoor head has its own controls, giving zoned heating and cooling.

claims.text: A heat pump makes the most financial sense when the air conditioner also needs replacing
claims.note: Incremental cost falls to $4,270 at AC failure and $370 when furnace and AC both fail (payback 0.6-1.1 years), versus 14.5-28.8 years with no failure.

claims.text: Heat pumps in mild climates can run without backup heat strips
claims.note: In mild southern climates a properly sized heat pump covers the design heating load without resistance backup.

claims.text: Incentives can make a heat pump cheaper upfront than a furnace and air conditioner
claims.note: Possible where large state or utility rebates stack, but in most of the US incentives narrow rather than reverse the upfront gap.

claims.text: Heat pumps give more even heating and cooling than furnaces and air conditioners
claims.note: Variable-speed heat pumps run longer at low output and even out temperatures, but single-stage units and poor installs do not.

claims.text: A heat pump raises a home's resale value
claims.note: Edwards notes in passing, citing other work, that homes with heat pumps may sell at a price premium.

claims.text: Replacing gas appliances with electric ones improves indoor air quality
claims.note: Unvented gas stoves measurably worsen indoor NO2 and are linked to asthma, but vented furnaces add little indoor pollution.

claims.text: Load management or smart panels let most homes electrify on 100-amp service without a service upgrade
claims.note: Load calculations and power-limiting devices often avoid upgrades, but some homes still need them and code acceptance varies.

claims.text: Backup resistance heat strips rarely run in a home with a heat pump
claims.note: Auxiliary resistance energy exceeded 40% of compressor heating energy at 5 of 11 all-electric sites and exceeded it at 2; every heat pump ran its auxiliary heater during or after defrost.

claims.text: Replacing a hot-water boiler with a heat pump takes more work than replacing a forced-air furnace
claims.note: Hydronic systems need air-to-water units or new distribution and often larger emitters, raising cost and complexity.

claims.text: In a new build a heat pump costs little more than a gas boiler, and skipping a gas connection can make it cheaper
claims.note: New builds avoid retrofit work and may avoid a gas connection, but the saving depends on the connection cost and design.

claims.text: Payback should count only a heat pump's extra cost over the system you would replace anyway
claims.note: Standard incremental-cost analysis compares against the replacement you would buy anyway when equipment is due.

claims.text: Most of a retrofit heat pump's cost is installation labour and radiators, so prices will fall little with scale
claims.note: Labour and soft costs dominate retrofit prices, but countries with mature markets show those costs can fall with scale and standard designs.

claims.text: A heat pump beats gas on running cost only when its COP exceeds the electricity-to-gas price ratio
claims.note: The break-even seasonal COP is the electricity-to-gas price ratio times the furnace AFUE (US 2024: 3.45 x 0.95 = 3.28), so the threshold is slightly below the raw price ratio.

claims.text: Landlords who don't pay utility bills have little reason to install efficient heating
claims.note: The split-incentive problem in rentals is well documented: owners who don't pay bills underinvest in efficiency.

claims.text: A ground-source heat pump pays back its extra cost within about a decade
claims.note: DOE's 5-10 year figure assumes favourable fuels and incentives; against gas without credits paybacks are often much longer.

claims.text: Ground-source heat pumps work efficiently in almost any climate because ground temperature is stable
claims.note: Ground temperatures a few metres down stay near the annual mean, so ground-source COP varies little with weather.

claims.text: Geothermal ground loops last for decades, far longer than the heat pump unit
claims.note: Polyethylene ground loops are rated for 50 years or more while the indoor unit typically lasts about 20 to 25 years.

claims.text: A home battery charged on cheap off-peak electricity cuts a heat pump's running cost
claims.note: A battery lets heating run on off-peak rates where time-of-use tariffs exist, but the battery's own cost usually outweighs the heating saving.

claims.text: Modern heat pumps run quietly
claims.note: Inverter heat pumps typically run around 40 to 55 dBA outdoors, comparable to or quieter than central AC units.

claims.text: A high-efficiency system pays back only if you stay in the home long enough to recoup its extra cost
claims.note: Savings accrue yearly, so a short ownership period may not recover a premium unless it is reflected in the sale price.

claims.text: Replacing equipment like-for-like is the cheapest installation option
claims.note: Switching system types adds gas lines, circuits or ductwork changes, so like-for-like swaps usually cost least upfront.

claims.text: Real-world heat pump efficiency is lower than manufacturers' rated figures
claims.note: Directly metered seasonal efficiencies of 152 mini-splits fell below their rated values on average, though some units met or exceeded their ratings; the evaluators blame usage patterns and test conditions, not misrated equipment.

claims.text: Heat pump prices vary mainly with system size and efficiency tier
claims.note: Capacity and efficiency tier drive equipment price, though installation complexity and contractor also move quotes.

claims.text: Major heat pump brands carry 10-year parts and compressor warranties
claims.note: Leading US brands offer 10-year limited parts warranties, usually conditional on registration.

claims.text: DIY-installable heat pumps cost far less than contractor-installed systems
claims.note: Pre-charged DIY units avoid much of the labour cost, but sizing, permits, warranty terms and electrical work limit the saving.

claims.text: Skipping heat pump maintenance raises its running costs
claims.note: Dirty coils and filters and wrong charge measurably reduce heat pump efficiency in field studies.

claims.text: If you are keeping a working furnace, a new air conditioner costs less upfront than a heat pump
claims.note: Edwards' national installed-cost medians are $4,684 for a central AC and $6,185 for a heat pump of the same size.

claims.text: A heat pump needs a heat loss calculation and system design to work well
claims.note: Field studies tie poor heat pump efficiency to bad sizing and emitter or flow design; a heat loss calculation is standard good practice.

claims.text: Ductless mini-splits may not distribute heat evenly through a whole house
claims.note: Because a mini-split heats one or two rooms, homes with a single-zone furnace found it hard to use as the primary heat without underheating the rest of the house.

claims.text: A heat pump shifts heating cost onto the electricity bill, which can rise sharply in winter
claims.note: UK households' electricity use rose 61% (3,080 kWh/yr) after a heat pump, concentrated in winter at over 200 kWh/week and near zero from April to October.

claims.text: Heat loss calculations for the same home can differ widely between surveyors
claims.note: Surveys rely on assumed U-values and ventilation rates, and comparisons of assessors show a wide spread for the same house.

claims.text: A heat pump hot water cylinder gives a more limited hot water supply than a combi boiler
claims.note: A cylinder stores a fixed volume and a heat pump reheats it more slowly than a combi boiler heats water on demand.

claims.text: Two-stage or variable-capacity heat pumps can be sized for heating without short cycling in cooling season
claims.note: Multi-stage and inverter units run at reduced capacity for cooling, limiting the short cycling and humidity problems of heating-based sizing.

claims.text: Inverter-driven heat pumps run long low-output cycles, which is easier on the compressor than short cycling
claims.note: Fewer starts reduce compressor wear and cycling losses; inverter units modulate to match load.

claims.text: A smaller furnace running longer uses about the same fuel as a larger one cycling on and off
claims.note: Fuel use is set by heat delivered and AFUE, not runtime; cycling losses make oversized units only slightly worse.

claims.text: Most gas furnaces also stop heating during a power outage
claims.note: Modern furnaces need electricity for ignition, inducer and blower, so they stop in an outage without backup power.

claims.text: State-run HEAR heat pump rebate funds can be exhausted soon after launch
claims.note: HEAR allocations are capped per state and several programs, including Colorado, reported funds committed within months of launch.

claims.text: Heat pump rebate programs involve heavy paperwork and long payment delays
claims.note: Program descriptions and contractor reports show multi-step applications and approval or payment queues of weeks.

claims.text: Heat pump rebates from utility, state and local programs can be stacked
claims.note: DOE highly recommends that states stack and braid HEEHR rebates with other programs and funding sources, but the statute bars combining them with another federal grant or rebate for the same project.

claims.text: Colorado offers a state tax credit for heat pumps installed in 2026
claims.note: Colorado's state heat pump credit continued into 2026 at a reduced amount under the state schedule.

claims.text: Zero-percent HVAC dealer financing builds its cost into the equipment price
claims.note: Dealer-fee financing is commonly priced into the installed cost, though not every promotional offer raises the price.

claims.text: The installed cost of a heat pump varies widely with the home, location and system type
claims.note: LBNL (642 heat pump installs, median $8,027): costs vary substantially by heat pump type (ground source nearly 3x others), and the main cost drivers were capacity, type, floor area, efficiency, climate zone, program and stories.

claims.text: Even in cold weather a heat pump delivers more heat per unit of energy than a fossil-fuel furnace
claims.note: Heat-pump-only cycles kept COP about 1.3 even at the 10F change point, while measured propane furnace cycles ran about 57-85% efficient.

claims.text: Heat pump reliability problems mostly come from poor installation
claims.note: Installation faults are common (DOE and NIST find most HVAC systems have at least one), but equipment defects and defrost problems also cause failures.

claims.text: A heat pump can often reuse a home's existing radiators and pipework with few changes
claims.note: Many UK homes need some radiator upsizing for low flow temperatures, but whole-system replacement is often unnecessary.

claims.text: Basic single-stage heat pumps are rated for heating only down to around freezing
claims.note: Single-speed heat pumps still produce heat below freezing but lose capacity quickly and usually need backup below balance points around 25-35°F.

claims.text: SEER and HSPF ratings do not fully capture a heat pump's real-world efficiency
claims.note: The report lists why measured SEER/HSPF fell short of ratings: test conditions (e.g. 80 F return air) do not represent real operation, plus cold-weather use, low-load operation, dry and fan modes, and long defrost periods.

claims.text: Installing a mini-split yourself saves thousands of dollars over a professional install
claims.note: Self-installing avoids labour markup, but refrigerant handling and warranty terms often require a licensed technician.

claims.text: Homes in places with temperature extremes need a secondary heat source alongside a mini-split
claims.note: The ductless unit's capacity fell to about 20% of rated below -20F, and the authors conclude these units should not be used without backup at extreme temperatures (below -15F).

claims.text: Most heating hours occur at moderate temperatures where heat pumps run most efficiently
claims.note: Bin-hour weather data show most heating hours fall at moderate temperatures, so seasonal COP sits closer to the mild-weather figure.

claims.text: Heat pumps need a correct refrigerant charge and a matched indoor coil to run efficiently
claims.note: Lab and field studies show refrigerant charge errors and mismatched coils cut heat pump capacity and efficiency, more so in heating.

claims.text: Outdoor heat pump units in cold climates must sit above the snow line
claims.note: Manufacturers require raised mounting in snowy climates so snow does not block airflow and defrost water can drain.

claims.text: Most US homes would save money over the equipment's life by switching to a heat pump
claims.note: With minimum-efficiency heat pumps, 7% discount rate and 15-year life, only 21% of US single-family houses would gain economically.

claims.text: The best heat pump lockout or balance-point temperature differs for every home
claims.note: The balance point depends on the home's heat loss and the unit's capacity curve, both of which vary by house.

claims.text: Heat pumps that need no backup heat at all are coming to market
claims.note: Some cold-climate units are installed without strips in moderate climates, but most cold-region installs still include backup heat.

claims.text: Most heat pumps are installed or sized improperly
claims.note: DOE and NIST field studies find most residential HVAC systems have at least one installation fault, though not all faults materially hurt performance.

claims.text: Heat pump incentives have drawn inexperienced installers into the market
claims.note: Program evaluations report quality problems from new entrants during incentive surges, but systematic data are thin.

claims.text: Heat pumps are easier than furnaces to size to the small heating loads of efficient homes
claims.note: Small inverter heat pumps and mini-splits come in capacities well below the smallest common furnaces.

claims.text: Comparing heat pump and gas running costs requires converting both to cost per delivered unit of heat
claims.note: The evaluators compare systems by the price per delivered Btu, combining each fuel's price, heat content and the appliance's efficiency (COP for the heat pump, AFUE for the furnace).

claims.text: Most US households would see lower energy bills with a heat pump
claims.note: Bills rise in 39% of homes with minimum-efficiency units and 5% with cold-climate high-efficiency units, so a majority save in every scenario, though fewer than a third of gas homes do with minimum units.

claims.text: A heat pump costs about the same as or less than a new furnace plus central air conditioner
claims.note: Edwards' median installed heat pump ($6,185) costs about $270 less than a gas furnace plus central AC and about $90 more than resistance plus AC, with over 80% of the cost distributions overlapping.

claims.text: Standard volumetric electricity rates overcharge heat pump owners for grid delivery costs
claims.note: In summer-peaking systems winter load adds little grid cost, so volumetric delivery charges overcharge heat pumps, but this fades as grids turn winter-peaking.

claims.text: Heat pumps using the phased-out R-410A refrigerant will cost more to repair as its supply shrinks
claims.note: The AIM Act phasedown has raised R-410A prices, but reclaimed supply will keep existing units serviceable for years.

claims.text: Cold-climate heat pumps are suitable for every US climate
claims.note: Cold-climate ASHPs proved beneficial in typical Minnesota homes, one of the coldest US climates, but needed backup heat, and the ductless unit should not be used without backup below -15F.

claims.text: High installation costs keep heat pumps from paying off for many households
claims.note: Higher upfront costs cut positive unsubsidized NPV to 41% and 21% for the more efficient units despite bigger bill savings; cost reductions are needed for almost half of households.

claims.text: Ductless heat pumps cut energy costs compared with ducted forced-air systems
claims.note: Ductless systems avoid duct losses, which are large when ducts run through unconditioned space, but vendor savings figures are not independently measured.

claims.text: Zoned ductless heat pumps save energy by heating only the rooms in use
claims.note: Heating fewer rooms uses less energy, but the saving depends on occupants actually setting back unused zones.

claims.text: Replacing an old oil furnace with a new oil furnace is a better choice than a heat pump
claims.note: In RMI's Providence model, heat pumps have a lower net present cost than heating-oil systems, as well as lower emissions.

claims.text: Heat pumps are inefficient where winter temperatures regularly fall near or below freezing
claims.note: In Maine, where winter temperatures are often well below freezing, 166 metered units averaged a seasonal heating COP of 3.15 including defrost, and 2 even at -10F.

claims.text: Heat pump water heaters use far less energy than conventional water heaters
claims.note: RMI models heat pump water heaters at a COP of 2.53-2.64 against 0.59-0.62 for gas, oil and propane water heaters, about four times the delivered heat per unit of energy.

claims.text: Heat pumps in cold climates may need a backup heat source on the coldest days
claims.note: With much of Minnesota below -10F design temperature, the heat pump is unlikely to meet the full load at all temperatures, making a backup heat source necessary.

claims.text: Switching to a heat pump saves more when it replaces an old, inefficient furnace
claims.note: Modeled cost savings were 40% replacing an 82% propane furnace versus 30% replacing a condensing propane furnace (metro), and 36% versus 26% in northern Minnesota.

claims.text: A heat pump's emissions fall over time as the electricity grid decarbonizes
claims.note: RMI expects the carbon benefit of heat pumps in California to grow as the grid moves toward 50% renewables by 2030, and expects Chicago's result to swing in favour as coal retires.

claims.text: Adding heat pump load in winter can lower electricity rates by using spare grid capacity
claims.note: In summer-peaking systems added winter sales spread fixed costs, but in winter-peaking regions heat pumps can drive new grid investment.

claims.text: Installers often set the dual-fuel switchover temperature higher than needed, reducing heat pump savings
claims.note: Practitioners and modelers report conservative default balance points, but systematic data on installed settings are limited.

claims.text: Federal tax credits were not a major driver of heat pump adoption
claims.note: Shipments held up after 25C ended and adoption tracks climate and prices, but the counterfactual is not measured.

claims.text: Even a full refrigerant leak from a heat pump has less warming impact than a year of burning oil or gas for heat
claims.note: A 2-5 lb R-410A charge is about 2-5 tCO2e, comparable to a gas furnace's annual emissions and below a typical oil boiler's.

claims.text: Ductless heat pumps cool more cheaply than window air conditioners
claims.note: Inverter mini-splits have seasonal efficiency ratings roughly twice those of typical window units.

claims.text: Federal IRA rebates can cover most or all of a heat pump's cost for low-income households
claims.note: HEAR allows up to 100% of cost capped at $8,000 for low-income households, but availability depends on each state's program.

commonlyWrong.text: Heating with a heat pump costs less than heating with a natural gas furnace
commonlyWrong.note: In the UK at 2024 prices on a standard flat tariff, heat pumps cost about £190 more per year to run than the gas boilers they replaced (boilers, not furnaces); only a heat pump time-of-use tariff reverses this.

commonlyWrong.text: A heat pump pays for itself through lower energy bills within a few years
commonlyWrong.note: Even over 16 years, unsubsidized NPV is positive for only 55% (minimum), 41% (medium) and 21% (high-efficiency) of homes, far from a few-year payback for all.

commonlyWrong.text: Heat pumps need a home to be well insulated to work economically
commonlyWrong.note: The UK Electrification of Heat trial installed heat pumps in every housing type, including old, poorly insulated homes, with similar efficiency; insulation lowers cost but is not a prerequisite.

commonlyWrong.text: Heat pumps need more maintenance or repairs than gas furnaces
commonlyWrong.note: Seven homeowners needed contractor visits, mostly minor control, sensor or condensate issues fixed in one visit, and the team judged this not atypical compared with their previous systems; the units were prototypes and the sample was small.

commonlyWrong.text: Heat pumps do not work in very cold climates
commonlyWrong.note: In monitored Minnesota homes cold-climate ASHPs cut heating costs 30-56%; cold weather raised backup and defrost use and lowered heat pump performance but overall system efficiencies remained high.

commonlyWrong.text: Most US homes would save money over the equipment's life by switching to a heat pump
commonlyWrong.note: With minimum-efficiency heat pumps, 7% discount rate and 15-year life, only 21% of US single-family houses would gain economically.

commonlyWrong.text: Federal Inflation Reduction Act rebates for heat pumps are available to most homeowners
commonlyWrong.note: DOE Program Notice 26-2: the federal electrification rebate no longer funds replacing non-electric (gas, oil, propane) heating, which rules out most homes that would switch to a heat pump; it is also an income-limited program run by the states.

commonlyWrong.text: Backup resistance heat strips rarely run in a home with a heat pump
commonlyWrong.note: Auxiliary resistance energy exceeded 40% of compressor heating energy at 5 of 11 all-electric sites and exceeded it at 2; every heat pump ran its auxiliary heater during or after defrost.

commonlyWrong.text: Backup resistance heat strips use less electricity than letting the heat pump run longer to catch up
commonlyWrong.note: The report says excessive auxiliary resistance runtime is costly and significant energy waste, to be minimized by proper heat pump sizing and controls (elsewhere it notes the auxiliary heater runs at COP 1).

commonlyWrong.text: A federal tax credit for heat pumps is available for installations in 2026
commonlyWrong.note: IRS fact sheet on the 2025 budget law (OBBB): the 25C home improvement credit is not allowed for property placed in service after December 31, 2025, and the 25D clean energy credit for expenditures after that date, so no federal heat pump credit applies to 2026 installs.

commonlyWrong.text: Heat pumps are inefficient where winter temperatures regularly fall near or below freezing
commonlyWrong.note: In Maine, where winter temperatures are often well below freezing, 166 metered units averaged a seasonal heating COP of 3.15 including defrost, and 2 even at -10F.

commonlyWrong.text: Home batteries charged off-peak pay back within a few years by cutting heat pump running costs
commonlyWrong.note: Independent estimates of home battery payback from tariff arbitrage are typically closer to a decade, not a few years.

commonlyWrong.text: Many heat pump owners end up with high bills and a colder house
commonlyWrong.note: Surveys of UK and US heat pump owners find satisfaction similar to or higher than gas boiler owners.

commonlyWrong.text: A premium inverter heat pump's energy savings repay its higher price over a basic single-stage system
commonlyWrong.note: Medium and high-efficiency variable-speed units save more on bills, but their higher upfront costs cut positive unsubsidized NPV from 55% (minimum single-speed) to 41% and 21% (38% if high-efficiency costs are overestimated).

commonlyWrong.text: Replacing an old oil furnace with a new oil furnace is a better choice than a heat pump
commonlyWrong.note: In RMI's Providence model, heat pumps have a lower net present cost than heating-oil systems, as well as lower emissions.

commonlyWrong.text: Switching to a heat pump cuts heating bills by half or more
commonlyWrong.note: In the UK, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump raised measured running costs by about £190/yr on a standard tariff, far from halving bills, even though energy use fell 40%.

commonlyWrong.text: Switching to a heat pump substantially lowers monthly energy bills
commonlyWrong.note: Edwards finds 19% of households would pay more and 28% show no clear change with a heat pump, so substantial bill cuts are not general.

commonlyWrong.text: Well-installed air-source heat pumps reach seasonal efficiencies around four in real homes
commonlyWrong.note: Across 166 metered indoor units of whole-home systems in Maine, the combined field-metered heating COP over the season was 3.15 including defrost, about 2 at -10F, not around four (a cold climate; milder climates would score higher).

claim.text: Air sealing and insulation should come before or alongside a heat pump
claim.note: ResStock modelling: envelope upgrades cut bill-increase cases (39% to 19% with minimum-efficiency units) and shrink heat pump capacity, but add about $9,000 so the net upfront cost rises, raising positive-NPV share slightly in cold climates and lowering it in warmer ones.

priorRecord.note: Reducing heat loss lowers the required heat pump size and running cost; DOE and retrofit programs recommend envelope work first, though it is not strictly required.

evidenceRecord.note: ResStock modelling: envelope upgrades cut bill-increase cases (39% to 19% with minimum-efficiency units) and shrink heat pump capacity, but add about $9,000 so the net upfront cost rises, raising positive-NPV share slightly in cold climates and lowering it in warmer ones.

claim.text: Cold-climate heat pumps often rely on backup resistance heat in the coldest weather, which raises bills
claim.note: Auxiliary heat runtime generally rose in colder bins and heavy use cut system COP over 30% at two sites, but the heavy users were undersized or faulty while six sites used little auxiliary heat.

priorRecord.note: Field studies in cold regions show strip heat use during cold snaps drives up winter electricity bills, especially with poor controls.

evidenceRecord.note: Auxiliary heat runtime generally rose in colder bins and heavy use cut system COP over 30% at two sites, but the heavy users were undersized or faulty while six sites used little auxiliary heat.

claim.text: Choosing a heat pump instead of a new central air conditioner adds efficient heating for little extra cost
claim.note: Wholesale heat pumps cost only $200-$500 more than equivalent ACs, but heat pumps sized to fully electrify heating often cost more to install than AC plus furnace because of larger capacity, wiring and panel upgrades.

priorRecord.note: A heat pump of the same capacity typically costs modestly more than an AC, and its heating displaces fuel or resistance heat.

evidenceRecord.note: Wholesale heat pumps cost only $200-$500 more than equivalent ACs, but heat pumps sized to fully electrify heating often cost more to install than AC plus furnace because of larger capacity, wiring and panel upgrades.

claim.text: Pairing a heat pump with rooftop solar makes it much cheaper to run
claim.note: Solar lowers the effective electricity price, but winter heating demand peaks when solar output is lowest, so the gain depends on net metering terms.

priorRecord.note: Solar lowers the effective electricity price, but winter heating demand peaks when solar output is lowest, so the gain depends on net metering terms.

evidenceRecord.note: In RMI's single Oakland retrofit scenario, a 6.5 kW solar array cut annual energy costs from $2,900 to $170 and brought net present cost below gas, but added over $15,000 upfront.

claim.text: Heating with a heat pump costs less than heating with a natural gas furnace
claim.note: In the UK at 2024 prices on a standard flat tariff, heat pumps cost about £190 more per year to run than the gas boilers they replaced (boilers, not furnaces); only a heat pump time-of-use tariff reverses this.

priorRecord.note: US modelling finds efficient heat pumps lower bills for many gas-heated homes, but where gas is cheap relative to electricity many see higher bills.

evidenceRecord.note: In the UK at 2024 prices on a standard flat tariff, heat pumps cost about £190 more per year to run than the gas boilers they replaced (boilers, not furnaces); only a heat pump time-of-use tariff reverses this.

claim.text: Oversized or poorly installed heat pumps cost more to run and deliver less comfort
claim.note: Field studies link poor sizing, charge, airflow and commissioning to substantially lower measured efficiency.

priorRecord.note: Field studies link poor sizing, charge, airflow and commissioning to substantially lower measured efficiency.

evidenceRecord.note: Units from one contractor with sloppy installs (up to 30 ft of excess coiled line set) ran 0.5-1.0 lower in COP at all temperatures, which rated efficiency cannot explain; the report adds that cooling oversizing of variable-speed units should not appreciably hurt efficiency.

claim.text: In cold climates a heat pump sized for the cooling load cannot carry the full heating load
claim.note: Sizing for heating added about one ton over cooling sizing; for an example home a 2-ton (cooling-sized) unit would hand off to the furnace at 27F versus 14F for 3-ton and 5F for 4-ton.

priorRecord.note: Single-speed units sized to cooling load fall short at design temperature, but variable-speed cold-climate units can be upsized for heating without short-cycling.

evidenceRecord.note: Sizing for heating added about one ton over cooling sizing; for an example home a 2-ton (cooling-sized) unit would hand off to the furnace at 27F versus 14F for 3-ton and 5F for 4-ton.

claim.text: Heat pumps need a home to be well insulated to work economically
claim.note: The UK Electrification of Heat trial installed heat pumps in every housing type, including old, poorly insulated homes, with similar efficiency; insulation lowers cost but is not a prerequisite.

priorRecord.note: The UK Electrification of Heat trial installed heat pumps in every housing type, including old, poorly insulated homes, with similar efficiency; insulation lowers cost but is not a prerequisite.

evidenceRecord.note: RMI says electric space heating is less suitable in inefficient buildings, especially in cold climates, yet its leaky retrofit homes in mild Houston and Oakland still had lower heat pump energy costs.

claim.text: Replacing an oil furnace with a heat pump pays back within a few years
claim.note: When an oil furnace needs replacing anyway, the incremental cost often pays back in about five to ten years, depending on oil prices and climate.

priorRecord.note: When an oil furnace needs replacing anyway, the incremental cost often pays back in about five to ten years, depending on oil prices and climate.

evidenceRecord.note: Fuel-oil homes switching to a heat pump usually take a private economic loss over 15 years at 7%; adoption above 20% is unlikely in cold climates on cost alone.

claim.text: A heat pump costs about the same as a central air conditioner of the same capacity
claim.note: Standard heat pumps usually cost modestly more than a same-size AC, while cold-climate variable-speed models cost several thousand more.

priorRecord.note: Standard heat pumps usually cost modestly more than a same-size AC, while cold-climate variable-speed models cost several thousand more.

evidenceRecord.note: NREL cost database: heat pump $2,994 base / $5,550 efficient versus central AC $3,164 / $5,180; the report says heat pumps cost very similar to split AC of the same SEER.

claim.text: Claiming a heat pump incentive requires proof that the installed equipment pairing meets the efficiency standard
claim.note: Federal and most utility incentives require the matched indoor and outdoor units to meet efficiency tiers, usually shown by an AHRI certificate.

priorRecord.note: Federal and most utility incentives require the matched indoor and outdoor units to meet efficiency tiers, usually shown by an AHRI certificate.

evidenceRecord.note: IRS 25C page: heat pumps must meet the CEE highest efficiency tier (and from 2025 carry a qualified manufacturer QMID on the return), but the page does not specifically require proof of the matched indoor/outdoor pairing.

claim.text: Well-installed air-source heat pumps reach seasonal efficiencies around four in real homes
claim.note: Across 166 metered indoor units of whole-home systems in Maine, the combined field-metered heating COP over the season was 3.15 including defrost, about 2 at -10F, not around four (a cold climate; milder climates would score higher).

priorRecord.note: Top installs reach seasonal COPs near four, but large field trials such as the UK Electrification of Heat project measured medians closer to three.

evidenceRecord.note: Across 166 metered indoor units of whole-home systems in Maine, the combined field-metered heating COP over the season was 3.15 including defrost, about 2 at -10F, not around four (a cold climate; milder climates would score higher).

claim.text: Running a heat pump steadily at low flow temperature costs less than heating in short bursts
claim.note: Monitored UK heat pumps reach higher COPs with weather compensation and continuous low-temperature running, though setbacks can still save in leaky homes.

priorRecord.note: Monitored UK heat pumps reach higher COPs with weather compensation and continuous low-temperature running, though setbacks can still save in leaky homes.

evidenceRecord.note: For variable-speed air-source units, 'set it and forget it' beats setbacks: homes without setbacks saved $10-$100 more a year; flow temperature (hydronic) is not studied.

claim.text: State and utility rebates can cover a large share of a heat pump's cost
claim.note: Some states and utilities pay thousands of dollars, but programs vary widely and many areas offer little.

claim.text: Burning gas in a power plant to run a heat pump delivers more heat than burning it in a home furnace
claim.note: RMI's water-heating example finds a heat pump water heater powered by a combined-cycle gas plant burns less gas and emits less than a gas-fired water heater, so burning gas at the plant is more efficient than burning it at home.

priorRecord.note: With about 40-50% plant efficiency, a seasonal COP above roughly 2-2.5 beats a condensing furnace, which most modern units achieve except in deep cold.

claim.text: A heat pump still uses less energy than resistance heat even in very cold weather
claim.note: Metered COP averaged 2 at -10F across 166 units in Maine homes, so even in very cold weather the heat pumps used about half the electricity resistance heat would.

claim.text: Inverter heat pumps keep far more of their heating capacity in cold weather than single-stage units
claim.note: AHRI performance data show variable-speed cold-climate units retaining 70-100% capacity at 5°F versus about half for basic single-stage units.

claim.text: Incentives can make a heat pump cheaper upfront than a furnace and air conditioner
claim.note: Possible where large state or utility rebates stack, but in most of the US incentives narrow rather than reverse the upfront gap.
