claim.text: Replacing gas appliances with electric ones improves indoor air quality
claim.note: Unvented gas stoves measurably worsen indoor NO2 and are linked to asthma, but vented furnaces add little indoor pollution.

priorRecord.note: Unvented gas stoves measurably worsen indoor NO2 and are linked to asthma, but vented furnaces add little indoor pollution.

evidenceRecord.note: Electrification is listed as improving health outcomes by reducing lung irritants such as nitrogen dioxide and PM2.5; a stated co-benefit, not measured.

claim.text: Backup resistance heat strips rarely run in a home with a heat pump
claim.note: Auxiliary resistance energy exceeded 40% of compressor heating energy at 5 of 11 all-electric sites and exceeded it at 2; every heat pump ran its auxiliary heater during or after defrost.

priorRecord.note: True in mild climates and with cold-climate units sized to the load; in cold climates with standard units backup heat runs a noticeable share of hours.

evidenceRecord.note: Auxiliary resistance energy exceeded 40% of compressor heating energy at 5 of 11 all-electric sites and exceeded it at 2; every heat pump ran its auxiliary heater during or after defrost.

claim.text: In a new build a heat pump costs little more than a gas boiler, and skipping a gas connection can make it cheaper
claim.note: New builds avoid retrofit work and may avoid a gas connection, but the saving depends on the connection cost and design.

priorRecord.note: New builds avoid retrofit work and may avoid a gas connection, but the saving depends on the connection cost and design.

evidenceRecord.note: RMI finds heat pumps usually the lowest-cost option in new construction because one device replaces furnace and AC, with avoided gas mains and service (median $8,800 per home) adding to the advantage.

claim.text: Most of a retrofit heat pump's cost is installation labour and radiators, so prices will fall little with scale
claim.note: Labour and soft costs dominate retrofit prices, but countries with mature markets show those costs can fall with scale and standard designs.

priorRecord.note: Labour and soft costs dominate retrofit prices, but countries with mature markets show those costs can fall with scale and standard designs.

evidenceRecord.note: For US ductless heat pumps, labour is commonly 30-35% of total cost (radiators do not apply to air-to-air systems).

claim.text: A heat pump beats gas on running cost only when its COP exceeds the electricity-to-gas price ratio
claim.note: The break-even seasonal COP is the electricity-to-gas price ratio times the furnace AFUE (US 2024: 3.45 x 0.95 = 3.28), so the threshold is slightly below the raw price ratio.

priorRecord.note: Break-even follows directly from energy prices per kWh and the furnace's efficiency; it is a standard calculation.

evidenceRecord.note: The break-even seasonal COP is the electricity-to-gas price ratio times the furnace AFUE (US 2024: 3.45 x 0.95 = 3.28), so the threshold is slightly below the raw price ratio.

claim.text: Modern heat pumps run quietly
claim.note: Inverter heat pumps typically run around 40 to 55 dBA outdoors, comparable to or quieter than central AC units.

priorRecord.note: Inverter heat pumps typically run around 40 to 55 dBA outdoors, comparable to or quieter than central AC units.

evidenceRecord.note: Two to four of 7-17 respondents per season reported noise, mostly louder indoor airflow than their furnace plus a vibration and a bad bearing, but noise never affected overall satisfaction.

claim.text: Replacing equipment like-for-like is the cheapest installation option
claim.note: Switching system types adds gas lines, circuits or ductwork changes, so like-for-like swaps usually cost least upfront.

priorRecord.note: Switching system types adds gas lines, circuits or ductwork changes, so like-for-like swaps usually cost least upfront.

evidenceRecord.note: Efficient heat pumps cost far more than like-for-like replacement, but a minimum-efficiency heat pump averaged $9,000 versus $11,000 for like-for-like furnace plus AC in cold-climate ducted homes with central AC.

claim.text: Heat pump prices vary mainly with system size and efficiency tier
claim.note: Capacity and efficiency tier drive equipment price, though installation complexity and contractor also move quotes.

priorRecord.note: Capacity and efficiency tier drive equipment price, though installation complexity and contractor also move quotes.

evidenceRecord.note: LBNL: ductless heat pump cost scaled near-linearly with capacity, but per-ton cost did not rise with HSPF or SEER and efficiency 'does not appear to be a strong driver of installed cost'; so size yes, efficiency tier no.

claim.text: Skipping heat pump maintenance raises its running costs
claim.note: Dirty coils and filters and wrong charge measurably reduce heat pump efficiency in field studies.

priorRecord.note: Dirty coils and filters and wrong charge measurably reduce heat pump efficiency in field studies.

evidenceRecord.note: Filters ran from clean to moderately dirty; one extreme filter cut fan airflow by 69%, but in testing even a very dirty filter shifted the airflow curve less than 10% versus clean, a small effect for typical neglect.

claim.text: Inverter-driven heat pumps run long low-output cycles, which is easier on the compressor than short cycling
claim.note: Fewer starts reduce compressor wear and cycling losses; inverter units modulate to match load.

priorRecord.note: Fewer starts reduce compressor wear and cycling losses; inverter units modulate to match load.

evidenceRecord.note: Despite variable-capacity compressors, the heat pumps were off for a significant fraction of the time at temperatures where continuous running was expected (thermostat schedules or controls); compressor wear was not studied.

claim.text: Even in cold weather a heat pump delivers more heat per unit of energy than a fossil-fuel furnace
claim.note: Heat-pump-only cycles kept COP about 1.3 even at the 10F change point, while measured propane furnace cycles ran about 57-85% efficient.

priorRecord.note: With a COP above 1 a heat pump delivers more heat per unit of site energy than a furnace, but per unit of primary energy or cost the edge narrows or reverses in deep cold.

evidenceRecord.note: Heat-pump-only cycles kept COP about 1.3 even at the 10F change point, while measured propane furnace cycles ran about 57-85% efficient.

claim.text: Basic single-stage heat pumps are rated for heating only down to around freezing
claim.note: Single-speed heat pumps still produce heat below freezing but lose capacity quickly and usually need backup below balance points around 25-35°F.

priorRecord.note: Single-speed heat pumps still produce heat below freezing but lose capacity quickly and usually need backup below balance points around 25-35°F.

evidenceRecord.note: The modelled minimum-efficiency single-speed heat pump keeps 47% of rated capacity at 5F and runs down to 0F, based on lab test data.

claim.text: Homes in places with temperature extremes need a secondary heat source alongside a mini-split
claim.note: The ductless unit's capacity fell to about 20% of rated below -20F, and the authors conclude these units should not be used without backup at extreme temperatures (below -15F).

priorRecord.note: Cold-climate units cope alone in many places, but backup heat is common practice where design temperatures fall below the unit's rated range.

evidenceRecord.note: The ductless unit's capacity fell to about 20% of rated below -20F, and the authors conclude these units should not be used without backup at extreme temperatures (below -15F).

claim.text: Outdoor heat pump units in cold climates must sit above the snow line
claim.note: Manufacturers require raised mounting in snowy climates so snow does not block airflow and defrost water can drain.

priorRecord.note: Manufacturers require raised mounting in snowy climates so snow does not block airflow and defrost water can drain.

evidenceRecord.note: Field staff found many outdoor units mounted with too little clearance, where roof melt and defrost water could freeze and impair the fan, and the manufacturer's guidance implies about four inches; this supports raised mounting but gives no 'snow line' rule.

claim.text: Most US homes would save money over the equipment's life by switching to a heat pump
claim.note: With minimum-efficiency heat pumps, 7% discount rate and 15-year life, only 21% of US single-family houses would gain economically.

priorRecord.note: NREL modelling finds most US households would see bill savings with efficient heat pumps, but gas-heated homes often see small or negative lifetime returns once installed cost is counted.

evidenceRecord.note: With minimum-efficiency heat pumps, 7% discount rate and 15-year life, only 21% of US single-family houses would gain economically.

claim.text: A heat pump costs about the same as or less than a new furnace plus central air conditioner
claim.note: Edwards' median installed heat pump ($6,185) costs about $270 less than a gas furnace plus central AC and about $90 more than resistance plus AC, with over 80% of the cost distributions overlapping.

priorRecord.note: Some programs find parity, but NREL/LBNL 2024 put medium- and high-efficiency heat pumps well above a furnace-plus-AC replacement.

evidenceRecord.note: Edwards' median installed heat pump ($6,185) costs about $270 less than a gas furnace plus central AC and about $90 more than resistance plus AC, with over 80% of the cost distributions overlapping.

claim.text: Zoned ductless heat pumps save energy by heating only the rooms in use
claim.note: Heating fewer rooms uses less energy, but the saving depends on occupants actually setting back unused zones.

priorRecord.note: Heating fewer rooms uses less energy, but the saving depends on occupants actually setting back unused zones.

evidenceRecord.note: Owners often heated or cooled only occupied rooms with the mini-split while the central system stayed low, which the evaluators say produces zonal savings not counted in their baselines; the effect was observed but not quantified.

claim.text: Adding heat pump load in winter can lower electricity rates by using spare grid capacity
claim.note: In summer-peaking systems added winter sales spread fixed costs, but in winter-peaking regions heat pumps can drive new grid investment.

priorRecord.note: In summer-peaking systems added winter sales spread fixed costs, but in winter-peaking regions heat pumps can drive new grid investment.

evidenceRecord.note: Electrification raises electricity sales, which helps pay for infrastructure and potentially puts downward pressure on retail rates.

claim.text: Federal IRA rebates can cover most or all of a heat pump's cost for low-income households
claim.note: HEAR allows up to 100% of cost capped at $8,000 for low-income households, but availability depends on each state's program.

priorRecord.note: HEAR allows up to 100% of cost capped at $8,000 for low-income households, but availability depends on each state's program.

evidenceRecord.note: Under the federal HEAR design, rebates could cover 100% of project costs up to $14,000 per unit, with up to $8,000 for a space-heating heat pump, for low- to moderate-income households; availability depends on each state's launch, and since mid-2026 fuel-switching no longer qualifies.

contested.text: Heat pump efficiency and capacity fall as the outdoor temperature drops
contested.note: Measured heat-pump-only cycles averaged COP about 1.3 at the 10F change point rising to 3.0-4.5 at 50-60F; outdoor temperature had the largest effect on COP across six Minnesota sites.

contested.text: Time-of-use or heat-pump electricity tariffs make heat pumps cheaper to run
contested.note: Staggered-adoption study of 6,631 UK households: switching to Octopus's Cosy heat pump time-of-use tariff saved about £318/yr (about 18% of the electricity bill), £78 from the tariff structure alone and £240 from shifting load; savings are vs the same supplier's flat tariff, and the authors are linked to Octopus.

contested.text: A heat pump costs more to buy and install than a gas furnace
contested.note: LBNL: among 2,298 HVAC measures, fuel-fired heating systems averaged $3,000 less than heat pump installations (heat pump median $8,027 vs furnace median $5,025 in 2019 dollars), though heat pumps also provide cooling.

contested.text: Heat pumps cut a home's carbon emissions compared with gas heating, even on today's grid
contested.note: On the 2024 UK grid, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump cut household energy CO2eq by about 1.16 t/yr, 36% of the pre-adoption footprint, from measured consumption changes and government emission factors.

contested.text: Heating with a heat pump costs less than heating with a natural gas furnace
contested.note: In the UK at 2024 prices on a standard flat tariff, heat pumps cost about £190 more per year to run than the gas boilers they replaced (boilers, not furnaces); only a heat pump time-of-use tariff reverses this.

contested.text: A heat pump costs less to run than heating with oil, propane or electric resistance
contested.note: Homes heating with electricity, oil or propane that have AC see lower bills in 95-100% of cases (median $300-$650/yr); 73-86% without AC; still 87-99% (propane) and 66-100% (oil) at 2019 prices.

contested.text: A dual-fuel system (heat pump with a gas furnace backup) is cheaper to run than either alone in cold climates
contested.note: With a well-set changeover temperature dual fuel can beat either fuel alone, but the saving over gas alone is small where gas is cheap and it needs two systems.

contested.text: Cold-climate heat pumps often rely on backup resistance heat in the coldest weather, which raises bills
contested.note: Auxiliary heat runtime generally rose in colder bins and heavy use cut system COP over 30% at two sites, but the heavy users were undersized or faulty while six sites used little auxiliary heat.

contested.text: Installing a heat pump can require costly electrical panel or service upgrades
contested.note: Across 21 installs, 38% needed a new panel, 24% a service line upgrade and 90% new breakers for auxiliary heat; electrical upgrades alone cost $3,750-$8,970 in labour and materials.

contested.text: Switching from gas to a heat pump raises the household's energy bills
contested.note: UK households switching from gas boilers see running costs about £190/yr higher on a standard tariff (about £83 after dropping the gas standing charge), so bills do rise modestly; but the same paper finds a heat pump time-of-use tariff saves about £318/yr, enough to reverse the rise.

contested.text: A heat pump can be added alongside an existing furnace to cut fuel use
contested.note: Mini-splits added alongside existing heating cut the baseline fuel by about 3.8-4.7 MMBtu per unit in winter 2016 on average, at a cost of about 763 kWh of electricity.

contested.text: A heat pump pays for itself through lower energy bills within a few years
contested.note: Even over 16 years, unsubsidized NPV is positive for only 55% (minimum), 41% (medium) and 21% (high-efficiency) of homes, far from a few-year payback for all.

contested.text: A heat pump still uses less energy than resistance heat even in very cold weather
contested.note: Metered COP averaged 2 at -10F across 166 units in Maine homes, so even in very cold weather the heat pumps used about half the electricity resistance heat would.

contested.text: Heat pumps last about as long as furnaces and air conditioners
contested.note: Heat pumps typically last 12-15 years, similar to central ACs but shorter than many gas furnaces.

contested.text: A heat pump costs about the same as a central air conditioner of the same capacity
contested.note: Standard heat pumps usually cost modestly more than a same-size AC, while cold-climate variable-speed models cost several thousand more.

contested.text: A heat pump costs about the same as or less than a new furnace plus central air conditioner
contested.note: Edwards' median installed heat pump ($6,185) costs about $270 less than a gas furnace plus central AC and about $90 more than resistance plus AC, with over 80% of the cost distributions overlapping.

contested.text: Heat pumps need a home to be well insulated to work economically
contested.note: The UK Electrification of Heat trial installed heat pumps in every housing type, including old, poorly insulated homes, with similar efficiency; insulation lowers cost but is not a prerequisite.

contested.text: Heat pumps need more maintenance or repairs than gas furnaces
contested.note: Seven homeowners needed contractor visits, mostly minor control, sensor or condensate issues fixed in one visit, and the team judged this not atypical compared with their previous systems; the units were prototypes and the sample was small.

contested.text: Heat pumps do not work in very cold climates
contested.note: In monitored Minnesota homes cold-climate ASHPs cut heating costs 30-56%; cold weather raised backup and defrost use and lowered heat pump performance but overall system efficiencies remained high.

contested.text: Ductless mini-splits may not distribute heat evenly through a whole house
contested.note: Because a mini-split heats one or two rooms, homes with a single-zone furnace found it hard to use as the primary heat without underheating the rest of the house.

contested.text: Federal Inflation Reduction Act rebates for heat pumps are available to most homeowners
contested.note: DOE Program Notice 26-2: the federal electrification rebate no longer funds replacing non-electric (gas, oil, propane) heating, which rules out most homes that would switch to a heat pump; it is also an income-limited program run by the states.

contested.text: Burning gas in a power plant to run a heat pump delivers more heat than burning it in a home furnace
contested.note: RMI's water-heating example finds a heat pump water heater powered by a combined-cycle gas plant burns less gas and emits less than a gas-fired water heater, so burning gas at the plant is more efficient than burning it at home.

contested.text: A federal tax credit for heat pumps is available for installations in 2026
contested.note: IRS fact sheet on the 2025 budget law (OBBB): the 25C home improvement credit is not allowed for property placed in service after December 31, 2025, and the 25D clean energy credit for expenditures after that date, so no federal heat pump credit applies to 2026 installs.

contested.text: Heat pump outdoor units are noisy enough to cause neighbour complaints
contested.note: Modern units are typically around 40-60 dB at a few metres and complaints are uncommon, though poorly placed units can bother neighbours.

contested.text: Switching to a heat pump cuts heating bills by half or more
contested.note: In the UK, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump raised measured running costs by about £190/yr on a standard tariff, far from halving bills, even though energy use fell 40%.

thinEvidence.text: Through 2025 a federal tax credit covered 30% of a geothermal heat pump's installed cost with no cap
thinEvidence.note: The 25D residential clean energy credit covered 30% of ground-source heat pump costs without a dollar cap until it ended after 2025.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps last about as long as furnaces and air conditioners
thinEvidence.note: Heat pumps typically last 12-15 years, similar to central ACs but shorter than many gas furnaces.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps on radiator systems often need larger radiators to run efficiently
thinEvidence.note: Heat pumps are efficient at low flow temperatures, so radiators sized for hot boiler water often need enlarging.

thinEvidence.text: Inverter-driven heat pumps run more efficiently and quietly than single-stage units
thinEvidence.note: Variable-speed compressors have higher SEER2/HSPF2 ratings and lower sound levels at part load.

thinEvidence.text: The UK Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant requires removing the existing gas boiler
thinEvidence.note: BUS rules require the heat pump to replace the fossil fuel system fully; hybrid systems are not eligible.

thinEvidence.text: Geothermal ground loops last for decades, far longer than the heat pump unit
thinEvidence.note: Polyethylene ground loops are rated for 50 years or more while the indoor unit typically lasts about 20 to 25 years.

thinEvidence.text: A ground-source heat pump pays back its extra cost within about a decade
thinEvidence.note: DOE's 5-10 year figure assumes favourable fuels and incentives; against gas without credits paybacks are often much longer.

thinEvidence.text: A heat pump removes the carbon monoxide risk of combustion heating
thinEvidence.note: An electric heat pump has no combustion, so it removes that carbon monoxide source, though other gas appliances may remain.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps give more even heating and cooling than furnaces and air conditioners
thinEvidence.note: Variable-speed heat pumps run longer at low output and even out temperatures, but single-stage units and poor installs do not.

thinEvidence.text: Radiator size and flow temperature decide whether a heat pump costs less to run than a gas boiler
thinEvidence.note: Larger emitters allow lower flow temperatures and higher COP, but the electricity-to-gas price ratio is just as decisive.

thinEvidence.text: Air-to-air heat pumps cost far less to install than air-to-water systems
thinEvidence.note: In the UK, ductless air-to-air installs typically cost a fraction of air-to-water systems with cylinders and radiator upgrades.

thinEvidence.text: Backup heat should be sized to cover the gap at design temperature, not the full heating load
thinEvidence.note: ACCA guidance sizes supplemental heat to the shortfall, though some codes or owners want full emergency backup.

thinEvidence.text: Colorado offers a state tax credit for heat pumps installed in 2026
thinEvidence.note: Colorado's state heat pump credit continued into 2026 at a reduced amount under the state schedule.

thinEvidence.text: Contractors discount replacing the furnace and air conditioner together
thinEvidence.note: Bundle pricing is a contractor practice with no independent data on its size.

thinEvidence.text: DIY-installable heat pumps cost far less than contractor-installed systems
thinEvidence.note: Pre-charged DIY units avoid much of the labour cost, but sizing, permits, warranty terms and electrical work limit the saving.

thinEvidence.text: Even a full refrigerant leak from a heat pump has less warming impact than a year of burning oil or gas for heat
thinEvidence.note: A 2-5 lb R-410A charge is about 2-5 tCO2e, comparable to a gas furnace's annual emissions and below a typical oil boiler's.

thinEvidence.text: Federal tax credits were not a major driver of heat pump adoption
thinEvidence.note: Shipments held up after 25C ended and adoption tracks climate and prices, but the counterfactual is not measured.

thinEvidence.text: The federal whole-home efficiency rebate still pays toward a heat pump that replaces gas heating
thinEvidence.note: HOMES is fuel-neutral and performance-based by design, but state availability and any 2026 changes are unverified.

thinEvidence.text: A gas furnace can run on a small generator during a power outage while a heat pump cannot
thinEvidence.note: A gas furnace's blower draws a few hundred watts, while a heat pump with strip heat needs several kilowatts at 240V.

thinEvidence.text: A geothermal desuperheater preheats domestic hot water using waste heat
thinEvidence.note: Desuperheaters recover compressor heat to preheat water, mainly during cooling season.

thinEvidence.text: Geothermal heat pumps rarely pay back their extra cost over an efficient air-source heat pump
thinEvidence.note: With modern cold-climate air-source units, the running-cost gap is small relative to the installation premium unless incentives are large.

thinEvidence.text: Geothermal heat pumps run best with little or no thermostat setback
thinEvidence.note: Manufacturers recommend minimal setback because recovery from deep setbacks can trigger backup heat and offsets savings.

thinEvidence.text: Heat loss calculations for the same home can differ widely between surveyors
thinEvidence.note: Surveys rely on assumed U-values and ventilation rates, and comparisons of assessors show a wide spread for the same house.

thinEvidence.text: A heat pump can often reuse a home's existing radiators and pipework with few changes
thinEvidence.note: Many UK homes need some radiator upsizing for low flow temperatures, but whole-system replacement is often unnecessary.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pump defrost cycles release meltwater that can ice driveways and walkways
thinEvidence.note: Defrost meltwater drains from the outdoor unit and can refreeze on paved surfaces in sub-freezing weather.

thinEvidence.text: A heat pump with an electric air handler costs less to install than a dual-fuel system with a furnace
thinEvidence.note: An air handler is usually cheaper than a furnace plus coil, but a dual-fuel retrofit that keeps a working furnace can cost less.

thinEvidence.text: A heat pump hot water cylinder gives a more limited hot water supply than a combi boiler
thinEvidence.note: A cylinder stores a fixed volume and a heat pump reheats it more slowly than a combi boiler heats water on demand.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pump incentives have drawn inexperienced installers into the market
thinEvidence.note: Program evaluations report quality problems from new entrants during incentive surges, but systematic data are thin.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pump outdoor units are noisy enough to cause neighbour complaints
thinEvidence.note: Modern units are typically around 40-60 dB at a few metres and complaints are uncommon, though poorly placed units can bother neighbours.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps are easier than furnaces to size to the small heating loads of efficient homes
thinEvidence.note: Small inverter heat pumps and mini-splits come in capacities well below the smallest common furnaces.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps that need no backup heat at all are coming to market
thinEvidence.note: Some cold-climate units are installed without strips in moderate climates, but most cold-region installs still include backup heat.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps need a correct refrigerant charge and a matched indoor coil to run efficiently
thinEvidence.note: Lab and field studies show refrigerant charge errors and mismatched coils cut heat pump capacity and efficiency, more so in heating.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps outsell gas furnaces in the US
thinEvidence.note: AHRI shipment data show air-source heat pump shipments exceeding gas furnace shipments each year since 2022.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps heat radiators to lower temperatures than gas or oil boilers
thinEvidence.note: Standard air-to-water heat pumps run most efficiently at 35-55°C flow versus 60-80°C for typical boilers, though high-temperature models exist.

thinEvidence.text: Heat pumps using the phased-out R-410A refrigerant will cost more to repair as its supply shrinks
thinEvidence.note: The AIM Act phasedown has raised R-410A prices, but reclaimed supply will keep existing units serviceable for years.

thinEvidence.text: A high-efficiency system pays back only if you stay in the home long enough to recoup its extra cost
thinEvidence.note: Savings accrue yearly, so a short ownership period may not recover a premium unless it is reflected in the sale price.

thinEvidence.text: Home batteries charged off-peak pay back within a few years by cutting heat pump running costs
thinEvidence.note: Independent estimates of home battery payback from tariff arbitrage are typically closer to a decade, not a few years.

thinEvidence.text: A home's true heating load can be estimated from smart thermostat runtime on a cold day
thinEvidence.note: Runtime-based load estimation is an established method for single-stage equipment, though less accurate for multistage or zoned systems.

thinEvidence.text: HVAC equipment prices keep rising, so waiting to buy a heat pump costs more
thinEvidence.note: HVAC equipment prices rose sharply in 2021-2025 with inflation and the refrigerant transition, but future prices and incentives are uncertain.

thinEvidence.text: HVAC replacement prices rose sharply in recent years
thinEvidence.note: Producer price indexes and refrigerant transitions drove double-digit HVAC equipment and install price increases since 2020.

thinEvidence.text: Installers can absorb heat pump rebates by raising their quotes
thinEvidence.note: Studies of energy-efficiency subsidies find some pass-through to sellers, but most rebate value usually reaches buyers.

thinEvidence.text: Installing a mini-split yourself saves thousands of dollars over a professional install
thinEvidence.note: Self-installing avoids labour markup, but refrigerant handling and warranty terms often require a licensed technician.

thinEvidence.text: Inverter heat pumps defrost faster than single-stage heat pumps
thinEvidence.note: Defrost behaviour varies by control strategy; no independent comparison is widely available.

thinEvidence.text: Inverter heat pumps run quieter than furnaces and older air conditioners
thinEvidence.note: Inverter outdoor units are quiet at low speed, but comparing them with mostly indoor furnaces is not like-for-like.

thinEvidence.text: Major heat pump brands carry 10-year parts and compressor warranties
thinEvidence.note: Leading US brands offer 10-year limited parts warranties, usually conditional on registration.

thinEvidence.text: Most federal home energy tax credit claims went to higher-income households
thinEvidence.note: CRS and Treasury data show residential energy credits were disproportionately claimed by households with incomes above $100,000.

thinEvidence.text: Most gas furnaces also stop heating during a power outage
thinEvidence.note: Modern furnaces need electricity for ignition, inducer and blower, so they stop in an outage without backup power.

thinEvidence.text: In off-grid homes a geothermal heat pump can cost less overall by shrinking the solar and battery system needed
thinEvidence.note: Based on one builder's modelled costs, not independently measured.

thinEvidence.text: Replacing a hot-water boiler with a heat pump takes more work than replacing a forced-air furnace
thinEvidence.note: Hydronic systems need air-to-water units or new distribution and often larger emitters, raising cost and complexity.

thinEvidence.text: Replacing HVAC equipment before it fails, in the off season, gets a lower price
thinEvidence.note: Planned replacement allows comparing bids and seasonal promotions, but discounts are anecdotal and vary.

thinEvidence.text: A smaller furnace running longer uses about the same fuel as a larger one cycling on and off
thinEvidence.note: Fuel use is set by heat delivered and AFUE, not runtime; cycling losses make oversized units only slightly worse.

thinEvidence.text: Standard volumetric electricity rates overcharge heat pump owners for grid delivery costs
thinEvidence.note: In summer-peaking systems winter load adds little grid cost, so volumetric delivery charges overcharge heat pumps, but this fades as grids turn winter-peaking.

thinEvidence.text: State-run HEAR heat pump rebate funds can be exhausted soon after launch
thinEvidence.note: HEAR allocations are capped per state and several programs, including Colorado, reported funds committed within months of launch.

thinEvidence.text: State and utility heat pump rebates were not affected by the 2025 federal budget law
thinEvidence.note: State and utility programs are funded separately (ratepayers, state budgets) and the budget law did not repeal them.

thinEvidence.text: Surveys showing heat pump owners are as satisfied as gas boiler owners rely on unrepresentative samples
thinEvidence.note: The Nesta survey groups differed in property type and were self-selected, though monitored trials also report high satisfaction.

thinEvidence.text: Variable-speed heat pumps dehumidify better than single-stage systems
thinEvidence.note: Longer low-speed run times can remove more moisture, but it depends on airflow settings and controls.

thinEvidence.text: Zero-percent HVAC dealer financing builds its cost into the equipment price
thinEvidence.note: Dealer-fee financing is commonly priced into the installed cost, though not every promotional offer raises the price.
